title: Host projections render the position packet; the per-system steward renderers and the steward guard registration are retired
summary: Breaking. @inventarch/compliance removes its projection role: renderHostArtifacts, renderWorkspaceProjection, admittedStewards, invalidAssessment, composeSteward, PROJECTION_MARKER, WORKSPACE_PROJECTION_MARKER, REQUIRE_STEWARD_PROFILES, STEWARD_HOST_TABLE and LEGACY_STEWARD_TOOLS, the HostArtifact, HostArtifacts, ProjectionMembership, RenderOptions, AdmittedSteward, Admission, WorkspaceProjectionInput and StewardComposition types, and the subpaths @inventarch/compliance/internal/projections, /internal/steward-profile and /internal/workspace-projection (exports and publish twins); the refusal code IA-COMP-PROJECTION-INVALID leaves COMP_CODES and CompCode. cite, fieldText, governanceClauses and text stay on @inventarch/compliance/internal/record-text. The position packet replaces them. ia host (and the install, update and remove refresh) renders the workspace's packet with the runtime's claude or codex adapter for the consumer target: .claude/rules/ia-workspace.md and .claude/skills/ia-authoring/SKILL.md for Claude, AGENTS.md and .agents/skills/ia-authoring/SKILL.md for Codex, each with the marker `<!-- Generated by ia project; edit the cited native records. -->`, and no .claude/agents/*.md file for any system. Before guard retirement or projection writes, the plan checks receipt and pending-evidence destinations, their directory ancestors, entry kinds and writability; a blocked directory or link is located at the actual path to repair. Each apply deletes the previous receipt before any projection file changes and last writes the receipt .ia/distributions/hosts/<host>-receipt.json (ia.packet-receipt.v1: the adapter's receipt plus cli, the CLI's id@version, removed, foreign, guard and writtenAt); ia host --remove deletes it. Digest-validated .ia/distributions/hosts/<host>-receipt-pending.json evidence preserves actual guard retirement and legacy file deletion hashes across an interrupted apply, so its successful retry records those effects in the receipt. Successful receipt publication consumes this evidence; a recorded final receipt digest recognizes a completed write if cleanup was interrupted. A later ordinary successful apply still reports only its own last-apply effects. ia doctor's projection rows now read it: a listed file missing (warn) or changed (fail), the receipt's packet digest against a fresh render (outdated, warn), and one info row listing removed and foreign files, which are not checked; a projection without a receipt, a 1.x one or an interrupted apply included, retains an unknown receipt row, while observed changed files also receive a failure row naming the file and its repair. The receipt-writing ia host <host> --apply remedy is offered when the projection has no blocking conflict; ia host plans the projection as an update. Upgrade path: both 1.x markers are owned and a 1.x projection state stays valid, so the next apply replaces the 1.x rules, AGENTS.md and skill files in place and deletes each .claude/agents/<name>.md file the state lists and that still carries its marker, listing it in the receipt's removed; an unmarked or unlisted agent file is never deleted and is listed foreign. A listed steward file edited by hand refuses as any owned file does. A linked .claude/agents directory is never traversed; recorded agent paths beneath it are foreign and left intact. Steward guard: ia host plans no hooks element and registers no guard any more (elements mcp, context, projection); with no steward subagents left a registered guard would deny every edit under .ia/src/systems/<name>/. Every projection apply, ia host --apply and --remove --apply and the install refresh, first retires a guard an earlier release registered (its group in .claude/settings.local.json and claude-guard-workspace.json, through @inventarch/distribution's guard-registration removal) before any projection file changes: the plan's projection element shows guard 'retire', the applied element guard 'retired', the human report says so, and an install, update or remove plan lists the hosts whose refresh retires one as retire, says so in the summary an apply confirms, and lists them as retired after the apply. An IA guard group in either .claude/settings.local.json or .claude/settings.json without matching local ownership refuses at that actual file before any steward changes, even when the ownership state is absent. The repair removes only the unmatched group and keeps unrelated hooks and settings. Retirement accepts an exact recorded owned group whose root is the workspace's old location; registration and execution keep their strict root checks. Install, update and remove previews expose each host's remove and foreign projection actions in text and projectionFiles JSON rows. A pending host journal takes priority in failure guidance and names its recover-* command before retry; a raw filesystem error names the actual writable-directory or file-lock repair instead of deleting an unrelated settings or temporary file. The repository generator also checks orphan guard groups and deletes only exact M4 steward bytes at their original paths; personal copies, edited files and unproven historical outputs remain untouched. The guard stays retired until generation-hook-governance re-keys it to `@mandate` scope, so system folders are unprotected meanwhile; the ia guard entry and @inventarch/steward-hook remain. @inventarch/cli/internal/host-projection exports applyHostProjection, ownsGuard, planRetirement, planFiles, preflightReceipt, readReceipt and HostProjectionApplied, and renderProjectionFor returns the adapter's {files, receipt}; @inventarch/cli/internal/host drops the hooks ElementId and adds AppliedElement, GUARD_RETIRED and STATE.receipt, with new GUARD_SCOPE and MACHINE_LOCAL texts; PlanView gains retire, retired and projectionFiles. @inventarch/distribution/guard-registration exports assertRetirableGuard for this preflight. @inventarch/distribution's projection planner writes only PROJECTION_PATHS (a .claude/agents path is refused as outside the allowlist), owns the two 1.x markers besides the caller's, accepts a listed agent path in a state for removal only, and names the ProjectionAction 'unowned' as 'foreign'. @inventarch/steward-hook protects a 1.x steward file only until it is removed: while the projection state lists it, or, with no state, while it carries a 1.x marker; any other agent file is the user's, and the receipt is protected with .ia/distributions/. @inventarch/runtime's PacketReceipt gains cli (left null by renderHost) and slug, the packet's provenance slug or null, and renderHost now prints each bare IA word token in free text, such as `@workspace`, as a code span and keeps an authored code span as written, so no rendered file shows a GitHub mention unless its author wrote the token touching a backtick; the packet, its digest and the entry count are unchanged. Limits: the receipt carries no source digests or per-command consumer versions; installed state stays unknown; workspace-runtime's distribution product projection is unchanged; the nine machine routes, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2, every ia scope form, body(K) and ia.position-body.v1 are unchanged.
